summary: queue() calls begin_turn() for every chunk, and begin_turn() unconditionally discards the turn's delivery-context-recorded flag, so a later chunk in the same turn erases proof that earlier delivered speech was committed to context.
failure_scenario: One turn with chunks c1, c2 queued one at a time (streaming.py:1612 queues each chunk inside the consumer loop after the previous one was played). c1 is played, mark_delivered_confirmed, then record_assistant_delivery -> consume_delivery_confirmation adds the turn to _delivery_context_recorded_turns (line 298). c2 is then queued: queue() -> begin_turn(turn_id) -> line 237 discard(turn_id). snapshot_turn_counts() at terminal time returns assistant_delivery_context_recorded=False although c1's text was recorded in the conversation context. That False value is forwarded to evidence admission (streaming.py:1739/1819 -> evidence/admission.py:3098 context_committed), giving a false 'no assistant context committed' terminal record for an interrupted or cancelled multi-chunk turn.
evidence: Read delivery.py and streaming.py:1596-1700. Ran a stdlib-only repro (stubbed package init): queue c1 with admission, mark_started, mark_delivered_confirmed, consume_delivery_confirmation -> snapshot flag True; queue c2 -> snapshot flag False. The only existing test, tests/speech/test_delivery.py:test_snapshot_turn_counts_is_frozen_text_free_and_precedes_close, queues both chunks before consuming the first, so it stays green and does not guard this. The discard belongs only in the closed-incarnation path.

summary: collect_environment_identity silently skips untracked files whose names git C-quotes, so the diffSha256 'exact candidate' identity omits them.
failure_scenario: Working tree has an untracked file with a non-ASCII name (e.g. e-acute.txt). `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` prints it as the quoted string "\303\251.txt" (core.quotepath default); Path(relative).is_file() is False, so the file is skipped and never fingerprinted. Editing that file leaves diffSha256 unchanged, so a bakeoff/characterization report claims an identical source identity for different bytes.
evidence: Ran git in a scratch repo: output was ['plain.txt', '"\\303\\251.txt"'] with is_file() -> [True, False]. No -z or core.quotepath=false is used. Limited to non-ASCII or special-character names, and the identity is advisory, so severity is low.

summary: _run_bakeoff_and_close's finally uses asyncio.gather on backend.close() without return_exceptions, so one failing close() replaces the completed (already paid-for) report with an exception.
failure_scenario: Metered bakeoff with tavily/exa/openai arms completes run_backend_bakeoff; then one backend.close() raises (e.g. network session teardown error). The exception in finally supersedes the returned report, main() never writes --output, and the metered lookups' results are lost.
evidence: Static reading of lines 580-592; not executed (aiohttp and other dependencies are unavailable offline here).

summary: Checked and found sound: word_boundary.py (gap search, cap and fade bounds), speech/types.py validation, segmentation.py (attempt and depth budgets, cancel and operation ownership, exact text/PCM preservation in qualified splits), delivery.py receipt identity binding and admission single-use, search_egress.py (binding generation, sequence idempotency and conflict, strict JSON parsing, admission lifecycle), current_facts.py egress controls (public-only resolver on RSS and page fetch, redirect revalidation, DTD/entity refusal, feed byte and element bounds, bounded executor with detached-call accounting; production host_launcher passes enrich_results=0, so arbitrary-site page extraction is not reachable), kokoro_worker.py (token-attested ready message, strict JSON frames, bounded PCM sizes, startup/fault/close ownership), moonshine.py (epoch/settling/close ownership), ollama.py, ollama_models.py and ollama_session.py (loopback-only origins, no-redirect and proxy-less transport, bounded reads, decision-schema refusal, identity re-checks, candidate close on failed commit), candidate_wheel.py (exact member set, RECORD/metadata binding to the source manifest) and profile_summary.py allowlist output.

Suspicions disproved or judged below the bar: (1) Moonshine cancel() raises an ExceptionGroup carrying an earlier unharvested add_pcm failure (reproduced), but backend.cancel still runs and state is reset, and the worker treats STT errors as terminal, so no wrong outcome; (2) Moonshine finish_utterance failing before backend.finish could leave stale native stream audio, but conversation/worker.py closes the session on that error, so unreachable; (3) kokoro_worker hashes model/voices by path and onnxruntime/kokoro-onnx later reopen the same path (hash-then-load gap), which needs same-user write access to the model directory, so it is speculative hardening; (4) ollama_models.installed_models uses a TaskGroup and could surface an ExceptionGroup instead of ValueError for one bad show payload, and I did not trace the route-level handler; (5) current_facts passage source_id can differ from the final rendered source position after outcome re-ranking, but only passage text is rendered or consumed (knowledge.py, knowledge_backends.py), so no attribution drift is observable; (6) AcceptedStartInferenceRequest already guarantees the accepted task is active, so the ollama.py next(...) cannot raise StopIteration.

Coverage gap: pytest and runtime dependencies (aiohttp, pydantic_core, numpy) are not installed and uv could not fetch them offline, so no suite was run; evidence is static reading plus small stdlib repros that stub the package init. Tests were skimmed for guard strength rather than read in full: tests/speech/*, tests/providers/test_ollama*.py, test_kokoro_worker.py, test_moonshine.py, test_current_facts.py, test_consent_bound_current_facts.py, test_search_egress*.py, test_codex_*.py, test_host_launcher_cli.py, test_provider_qualification.py, test_natural_work_scenario.py, test_foreground_knowledge_benchmark.py and test_profile_summary.py were NOT audited line by line. scripts/qualify_*.py, owned_close_faults_worker.py and the orchestration they call (candidate_source_archive_oracle, qualification registrations, tests.integration helpers) were read only at their call surface; whether the packaged-process worker imports tests.integration.* from the source tree rather than the verified wheel was not traced. Windows-only behavior (SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE, OpenProcess parent watchdog, Job containment) was not exercised.
